title: Init - one call that brings the whole tool online and reports what works
description: The single entry point an agent calls once at the start of a session instead of probing the installation by hand. It loads the configured env file, brings the local SearXNG up (unless told to skip it), and finishes with a full doctor sweep, then answers the only question the caller has: can I search now, and with what. A standalone orchestration over the searxng and doctor contracts; it emits the same Envelope (meta.layer "init") as every other command.

searxng.description: 'up' installs (first run only) and starts the local SearXNG, then points this process at it. 'skip' leaves it alone: an already-configured WEBSEARCH_SEARXNG_URL is still used and still checked.

quick.description: Run the doctor sweep in quick mode: no per-engine fanout, extra tools, or fetch tiers. Faster, but the capabilities those checks decide come back 'unknown'.

timeout_ms.description: Per-check network timeout for the doctor sweep. Not a budget for the whole call: a first SearXNG install clones a repository and builds a virtualenv.

tor.description: auto starts Tor only when the tor layer is on, which it is not unless you turned it on. skip leaves it alone. There is no 'up' here on purpose: bringing up an anonymity layer nobody asked for would change where every request in the session comes from.

InitStep.description: One stage of the bring-up, in the order it ran. A step never aborts the run: a SearXNG that will not start is a warn, because the keyless engines still search.

summary.description: One line, safe to print: never carries credentials.

detail.description: Free-form, step-specific facts (paths, versions, counts). Additive by contract. Variable NAMES only, never their values.

hint.description: What to do about a warn or fail.

CapabilityStatus.description: What the caller can rely on for one capability. 'ok' works now; 'degraded' works but something asked for is missing; 'down' does not work; 'off' is an optional layer nobody turned on, which is the default and not a problem; 'unknown' was not probed this run (quick mode).

InitCapabilities.description: The answer to 'what can I use'. Read this instead of re-deriving it from the doctor checks.

InitEngines.description: Which providers answered this run. A silent provider is normal: the fanout rotates and fuses whatever responds.

silent.description: ddgs providers that returned nothing (blocked, rate-limited, or a stale parser).

reached_via_searxng.description: Silent providers that the local SearXNG did reach with its own parser. Query these through SearXNG.

searxng_engines_active.description: Engines enabled in the local SearXNG instance, when one is answering.

InitPayload.description: Envelope.data for an init run. Envelope.ok reports whether the bring-up RAN; 'ready' reports whether the tool is online. A run that finds everything broken is still ok:true with data.

ready.description: True only when state is 'ready'. This is the flag to wait on: everything asked for is online.

state.description: 'ready': search, fetch and the extra tools work, and SearXNG is up when it was asked for. 'degraded': search works, but something asked for is missing (SearXNG down, or a failed check). 'broken': search itself does not work.

headline.description: One line stating what is online, safe to read out verbatim.

next_actions.description: What to do about anything not online, already deduplicated. Empty when state is 'ready'.

doctor.description: The full sweep this run finished with, so the caller never needs a second diagnostic call.

InitResponse.description: An Envelope whose meta.layer is "init" and whose data is an InitPayload (or null on error).
